name: Advanced Seminar Innovation & Entrepreneurship: Innovation and Organization Design
description:
Please read the attached Syllabus for detailed information on the seminar and expectations. 
Attendance to 3 course sessions in Garching is required: 17 October 2023 (kick-off), 31 October 2023, 30 January 2024 (final presentation).
Please e-mail lecturers and attend the kick-off if you have not been allocated a seat but would like to participate!

This seminar prepares students for their Master’s thesis. The students will write a seminar paper on a specific topic of their own choosing, present this topic to the class, discuss a fellow student's paper, and be involved in academic discussions on a variety of topics. The seminar thus equips the participants with concepts, methods, and thinking patterns needed and applied by both managers and academics in the fields of innovation, organization, and strategy – as well as the ability to utilize them with and without preparation.

Accordingly, students may choose from a broad range of topics around the development of new and established businesses, the strategies managers devise and execute including questions of positioning, and the organizational design choices they have to deal with. Potential questions you may study include: 
How are new businesses created and how do they evolve? 
How do their structures develop and change? 
Are there different paths to consistent configurations and if yes, how do they differ from each other? 
What role do supposedly more novel approaches to conducting business (ecosystems, crowdsourcing, open innovation…) or funding companies (incubators, crowdfunding…) play, when should be used, by whom, and how? 
How does the business environment influence the decision-making of new or established ventures, such as through membership in categories? 

Students may choose from a range of topics and write their paper in this context (see Syllabus for more details and a preliminary list of topics), but may suggest their own topic as well. In any case, and as we will elaborate in the course, these topics are just the starting point for identifying a more specific research question and investigate this as your own research project.
prerequisites: Good English language skills are required. Students should also have an understanding of basic principles of entrepreneurship, strategy, and organization as well as empirical research methods.
